speakers.name: Dr. Rajendra Prasad
speakers.positionSummary: Manages both the Rules Committee programme and the continuing Objectives Resolution debate, balancing time, holidays and the Assembly's unfinished preliminary business.

speakers.name: Ananthasayanam Ayyangar
speakers.positionSummary: Asks that the Assembly take the full Christmas week as holiday and resume in the new year.

speakers.name: Hriday Nath Kunzru
speakers.positionSummary: First raises scheduling concerns, then argues that postponing the Objectives Resolution can increase the Assembly's moral authority and widen participation without delaying real constitutional work.

speakers.name: Dhirendra Nath Datta
speakers.positionSummary: Argues members need time to study and amend the Rules; later interjects sceptically during Gopalaswami Ayyangar's proposal.

speakers.name: J. J. M. Nichols-Roy
speakers.positionSummary: Defends the Resolution as democratic, protective of religious freedom and minorities, and capable of accommodating autonomous units and later participation.

speakers.name: Debi Prasad Khaitan
speakers.positionSummary: Urges members to give the Constituent Assembly and completion of its rules precedence over other engagements.

speakers.name: Mohan Lal Saksena
speakers.positionSummary: Suggests altering the sitting schedule so the Rules Committee can finish and the House can begin consideration sooner.

speakers.name: R. K. Sidhwa
speakers.positionSummary: Rejects British minority propaganda, cites Parsi experience as evidence against separate electorates and insists the Assembly should proceed.

speakers.name: Purushottam Das Tandon
speakers.positionSummary: Notes scheduling constraints and argues members and parties need adequate time to study the Rules before the House takes them up.

speakers.name: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
speakers.positionSummary: Argues the Assembly's business must take precedence and the Rules should be completed before the preliminary session disperses.

speakers.name: K. Santhanam
speakers.positionSummary: Suggests placing completed portions of the Rules before the House rather than waiting for the whole draft.

speakers.name: Sri Biswanath Das
speakers.positionSummary: Defends the Resolution's treatment of grouping, popular sovereignty and the States, and rejects the claim that the Assembly is a caste-Hindu body.

speakers.name: N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar
speakers.positionSummary: Opposes adjournment, asserts broad constituent power, proposes a route on grouping and argues that authority in Indian States must ultimately derive from their people.

interventions.summary: The Chairman reports progress in the Rules Committee and proposes completing the preliminary session's essential work, including rules and committees, despite the approaching Christmas week.
Ananthasayanam Ayyangar asks for the whole Christmas week as holiday before the Assembly resumes in the new year.
Kunzru says members had reasonably expected the session to finish before Christmas and asks the Chair to respect prior public engagements when fixing the next sitting dates.
Datta argues that members need several days to study the Rules and prepare amendments, making immediate post-Christmas consideration impractical.
Nichols-Roy explains the importance of Christmas holidays to Christian members and supports resuming in early January.
Khaitan argues that Constituent Assembly work must take precedence and that the House should not disperse before completing essential procedure.
Saksena proposes giving the Rules Committee more uninterrupted time and adjusting the House schedule so the completed report can be considered sooner.
Sidhwa counters that members and party groups need adequate time to study the report and submit amendments before voting on the Rules.
Patel says it is impossible to suit every member's engagements and insists that the Assembly finish the Rules before dispersing.
interventions.excerpt: precedence should be given to the work of the Constituent Assembly

interventions.summary: Santhanam suggests taking up Rules piecemeal as drafts become ready; the Chairman rejects the idea and says they should be considered as a whole.

Tandon argues against taking up the Rules during Christmas week because members and parties need time to digest them and prepare amendments. The Chair defers a final scheduling decision to the next day.

Nichols-Roy supports the Resolution as a democratic programme, defends autonomous units, justice and freedom of religion, and rejects the claim that constitution-making by this Assembly amounts to a Hindu Raj.
interventions.excerpt: a constitution to be made by the people of India

interventions.summary: Sidhwa uses the Parsi experience to reject British claims that minorities require externally imposed communal safeguards, denounces separate electorates and says the Assembly should continue its work.

Biswanath Das supports the Resolution, argues that omission of the word 'group' leaves future arrangements open, defends popular sovereignty in the States and rejects descriptions of the Assembly as a caste-Hindu institution.

Kunzru argues that Jayakar's amendment is intended to facilitate rather than obstruct constitution-making. A short postponement, he says, could improve participation and moral authority without materially delaying the Assembly's work.

Gopalaswami Ayyangar urges the House to complete the Resolution during these sittings, arguing that an objectives declaration should guide constitution-making from the beginning rather than be postponed until the end.
Datta briefly interjects during Gopalaswami Ayyangar's discussion of a possible grouping resolution.
interventions.excerpt: Please save us from such prayerful resolutions!

interventions.summary: Gopalaswami Ayyangar proposes that the Assembly itself consider modifying the grouping-vote rule rather than rely on a Federal Court reference, and stresses that the Assembly possesses powers necessary to accomplish its constituent task.

He answers objections from princely States, argues that real authority must derive from the people even where a hereditary ruler remains, and envisages responsible constitutional government in the States within the future Union.
interventions.excerpt: all powers of Government ... should be deemed to be derived from the people

interventions.summary: At 1:15 PM the Chairman adjourns the House until 11 AM on 19 December.
